column4: “BISITA SELDA” Legal Support for Muslim PDLs (Persons Deprived of Liberty)
column5: National Commission on Muslim Filipinos
column6:
Bisita Selda is a comprehensive and responsive program to address the needs of the Muslim PDLs (Persons Deprived of Liberty) by providing access to free legal assistance and other related services.
 
This program is in line with the mandate of the Commission under Republic Act No. 9997 "to preserve and develop the culture, tradition, institutions, and well-being of Muslim Filipinos..." and the specific mandate of the Bureau of Legal Affairs "to provide Muslim Filipinos with legal education and assistance in case of litigation involving their persons or interests..."

The program is consistent with the Philippine Development Plan 2023-2028 of President Ferdinand "Bongbong" R. Marcos, Jr., under Subchapter 13.2 Enhance Administration of Justice, to wit: 

Outcome 1: Quality and efficiency in disposition of cases improved 
Outcome 2: Access to quality free or affordable legal services by Filipinos improved
Outcome 3: Quality of life of PDL improved, and productive re-integration of PDL in the community ensured (emphasis supplied)

Bisita Selda is a re-calibrated version of the Legal Support for Detainees Program (LSDP) of the NCMF Bureau of Legal Affairs.

column4: TWO (2) STOREY PDL DORMITORY WITH ROOF DECK at LRP (10.0m x 50.0m)

column6:
The Bureau of Corrections is committed to operating a safe and secure prison system, while providing prison-based treatment programs. As a commitment to achieve the BUCOR’s mandate to rehabilitate, maintain and safekeep national offenders, provision of adequate and appropriate facilities is our priority. 
The Leyte Regional Prison now safe keep more than Four Thousand (4000+) PDL who are confined in different dormitories of Maximum, Medium and Minimum-Security Compounds – giving a total congestion rate of around 600%. Due to the present congestion of the prison’s facilities, some PDLs are given no choice but to share their bed space just to accommodate other PDLs while other PDL occupy the hallways.

As per the Master Decongestion Plan of BuCor-NHQ, LRP is expected to receive two thousand (2,000) PDL before the end of each year from 2023 until 2028.

column4: Protecting the Rights of Women and Children (PRO- Women and Children)
column5: Department of the Interior and Local Government
column6:
In adherence to the directives of the Justice Sector Coordinating Council (JSCC) and in alignment with its mission to enhance the capabilities of local government units in effectively providing essential services to the populace, including social protection services and justice administration, the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) intends to propose a project, titled: "Protecting the Rights of Women and Children (PRO-Women and Children).

This initiative aims to strengthen the capacities of local justice sector actors in safeguarding the rights and ensuring access to justice of vulnerable groups, especially women and children. This will be achieved by heightening their understanding of pertinent laws and issues pertaining to women and children, as well as familiarizing them with local protocols and procedures for handling such cases. To sustain the Department’s ongoing efforts, this project will leverage the accomplishments of the DILG's previously locally funded project, "Advocacy and Capacity Building of Local Mechanisms on Women and Children" in 2022, utilizing its advocacy materials and training manuals. 

The project aligns with the national objectives outlined in the Philippine Development Plan 2023-2028, specifically Sub-Chapters 2.3 (Establish Livable Communities) and 3.2 (Strengthen Social Protection), which emphasize the reinforced enforcement of laws safeguarding women and children, along with fostering social cohesion to advance the welfare of vulnerable groups and mitigate acts of violence against them.

column4: Regional Prison Facilities Design and Build Project of San Ramon Prison and Penal Farm
column5: Bureau of Corrections
column6:
The Regional Prison Facility Design and Build Project of San Ramon Prison and Penal Farm (SRPPF) is a multi-year infrastructure initiative aimed at modernizing and expanding the country’s correctional system. This project involves the construction of a state-of-the-art prison complex at Camp Pilar Site, Curuan, Zamboanga City, in line with the government’s commitment to decongest existing facilities and provide secure, humane, and rehabilitative incarceration for Persons Deprived of Liberty (PDL).
Key components of this project include the establishment of typical facilities such as maximum, medium, and minimum prison security compounds; specialized prison compounds for Muslim offenders to address their unique cultural and religious needs; and a Correctional Institution for Women (CIW) to cater to female PDL with gender-sensitive rehabilitation programs. Each compound will be allotted 10 hectares, designed to accommodate modern security features, sustainable infrastructure, and comprehensive rehabilitation programs to support the successful reintegration of PDL into society.

column4: Building and Operating a Halfway House for Clients of Parole and Probation Administration - Region IV-B (MIMAROPA)
column5: Parole and Probation Administration
column6:
The Transitional Living Halfway House is a structured residential reentry program designed to support inmates and parolees as they reintegrate into the community following incarceration.  The project provides a safe supervised and rehabilitative environment that bridges the gap between correctional facilities and independent living its mission is to reduce recidivism, promote personal responsibility and support long-term stability through evidence-based services and community partnerships.  

Individuals leaving incarceration frequently face significant barriers including homelessness, unemployment, limited life skills, substance use disorders, and stigma.  Without adequate support these challenges can lead to repeated cycles of incarceration.

The halfway house aims to address these needs by offering a stable living environment, targeted programming and coordinated services intended to improve residents' outcomes and enhance public safety.

column4: CONSTRUCTION OF ADMINISTRATIVE AND REFORMATION FACILITIES AT SRPPF
column5: Bureau of Corrections
column6:
The construction and rehabilitation of administrative and reformation facilities at the San Ramon Prison and Penal Farm (SRPPF) aim to strengthen institutional capabilities by providing safe, durable, and functional structures that support efficient operations and effective service delivery. Using composite materials such as reinforced concrete and structural steel, the project will upgrade key facilities including administrative offices, court rooms, the powerhouse, and the motor pool building. These improvements will ensure resilience against heavy usage and environmental conditions, while creating an organized and secure environment conducive to streamlined workflows, enhanced coordination, and improved overall management of prison operations.
For the reformation component, the project will establish and enhance aquaculture and livestock facilities, classrooms, and multi-purpose training halls designed to support the holistic rehabilitation of Persons Deprived of Liberty (PDL). The use of modern construction materials ensures that these facilities are safe, long-lasting, and adaptable to various vocational and educational programs. By providing conducive spaces for skills training, values formation, and livelihood development, the improved infrastructure will help equip PDL with competencies necessary for reintegration, while supporting SRPPF’s goal of becoming a model for humane and transformative corrections.

column4: Lupong Tagapamayapa Incentives Awards (LTIA)
column5: Department of the Interior and Local Government
column6:
The Lupong Tagapamayapa Incentives Awards or LTIA, established by the Department in 1982, consistent with Section 406(b) of Republic Act 7160 (The Local Government Code of 1991) aims to recognize Lupong Tagapamayapas for their outstanding contributions to attaining the objectives of the Katarungang Pambarangay (KP). Said award system was elevated as a Presidential Award by virtue of Executive Order No. 394, s. 1997, that, until today, has been seen as an avenue for our barangays to deliver efficient justice administration that is able to resolve legal disputes within the justice system in our local communities.

Said program also responds to Chapter 13 of the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023-2028, entitled Ensure Peace and Security and Enhance Administration of Justice. Through the LTIA, the Department is able to support the promotion of an efficient administration of a justice system, may it be traditional or alternative that inspires integrity, fairness, and accountability in our communities. Relatedly, the challenges laid out in Subchapter 13.2, Enhance Administration of Justice of the PDP 2023-2028, call for a need for coordinated action to enhance justice administration through the provision of cost- and time-effective dispute resolution mechanisms.

In 2024, the LTIA Program received recognition and support through the virtue of Executive Order No. 68, s. 2024, "Strengthening the LTIA
System and Reorganizing the National Awards Committee" which also expanded the number of categories from four (4) to eight (8).

column4: Expansion & Decongestion of Cagayan de Oro City Jail
column5: Bureau of Jail Management and Penology
column6:
The current jail facility has long been operating beyond its intended capacity, leading to overcrowding, compromised security, and inhumane living conditions for PDL. This congestion has resulted in numerous challenges, including increased tension among PDL, difficulty in PDL classification, higher risks of disease transmission, and limited access to rehabilitation and legal services.
To address this urgent issue, the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology Region Office - X (BJMPRO-X), has made a proposal for the construction of a 3-storey jail building consisting of 36 standard detention cells. This new facility will significantly expand PDL housing capacity and improve the overall living and operational conditions in the jail.
